name: Updater Services Ltd
title: Updater Services Ltd - 543996 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Facilities and BSS services business with 9% revenue growth to INR764 crores and 5.5% EBITDA margin; no capacity or capex story, growth is labour-led and pass-through, with weak IFM margin of 4.5%.

triggers.label: Matrix EBGC gross margin ~21% vs 12% a year ago
triggers.quote: Q1 this year, we are at about 21%.

triggers.label: No formal guidance given
triggers.quote: We normally don't give formal guidance.

red_flags.quote: in Avon in the last quarter, there was a restatement as you know.

red_flags.quote: that deal is on hold because there are differences in terms of valuation.

summary.headline: Updater Services Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR764 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR42 crore (5.5% margin) and PAT of INR30.3 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 9% YoY to INR764 crore, with IFM up 11% to INR525 crore and BSS up 7% to INR253 crore. Consolidated EBITDA was INR42 crore at a 5.5% margin, with IFM at 4.5% (about INR24 crore) and BSS at 7.5% (about INR19 crore). Management declared an interim dividend of INR1 per share, about INR7 crore of cash outflow, and said it remains a net cash company. Management gave no formal guidance and pointed to Q1 as the indicator.

financial_highlights.change: +9% YoY vs INR700 crore in Q1 FY26
IFM PAT INR20.7 crore vs INR19.9 crore a year ago

segments.name: IFM (Integrated Facility Management, incl. Global and Avon)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR525 crore, up 11% YoY, with 6 new significant logos added. EBITDA about INR24 crore at 4.5% margin, with management noting this is stable and it does not expect further decline. Global reported its highest-ever EBITDA margin of 9% (vs 5% last year), and all 23 airports are operational. Avon core mailroom revenue grew 10% YoY after the transport business was fully shut off.

segments.name: BSS: Denave (sales enablement)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR161 crore, up 18% YoY, with EBITDA INR7 crore at 4.3% margin. Margin pressure came from a mix shift toward low-margin field marketing and budget timing at one large customer.

segments.name: BSS: Athena (BFSI customer engagement)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR28 crore with EBITDA INR5 crore, an 18% margin. Won 2 new clients that started in July on 2-year tenures, and started its first agentic AI engagement in May-June.

segments.name: BSS: Matrix (Audit & Assurance and EBGC)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 2% YoY and was flat QoQ. EBITDA rose about 76%, and margin improved to 13.1% from 7.6% (EBITDA INR4.2 crore vs INR2.4 crore). EBGC revenue grew 9% YoY to INR12.5 crore with gross margin about 21%. Audit & Assurance revenue fell about 2% as large audits slipped from May into June and July.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; management said Q1 numbers can serve as an indicator.
Management expects IFM and BSS each to grow low double digits, roughly 9-12%, so the 67:33 IFM:BSS mix should hold.
Matrix Audit & Assurance results are expected in H2 FY27 as deferred audits land.
EBGC volumes and margins are expected to be sustainable through this year.
Cash of upwards of INR300 crore to be deployed across inorganic growth, brownfield organic investment and shareholder returns.
capex_capacity: Global: all 23 airports operational and generating revenue; expanding into training and aviation support services, including security training and regulatory certification.
Athena: another agentic AI project has customer approval and is expected to go live in August 2026.
Matrix: a dedicated sales team was built for Audit & Assurance to target large multinational audits and food and automobile sectors.
Acquisition: a pending deal is on hold over valuation differences; management said it is also reviewing a wider pipeline.
Labour: recruitment teams in Eastern and Northeast India redeploy workers to labour-short states such as Gujarat, parts of Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and NCR.
demand_pricing: IFM demand: strong commercial real estate, GCC expansion and enterprise outsourcing; management sees clients favouring single strategic partners. Management says its GCC exposure is limited (low commercial, no residential).
BSS demand: clients are prioritising projects with faster ROI and sales productivity; spending is selective in some global markets.
EBGC: volumes are recovering after subdued banking and BPO hiring; the company describes margins as volume-driven with a flat cost base.
Contracts are largely pass-through, and labour shortages in several states did not visibly hit Q1 results.
Seasonality: Q1 is seasonally weak for catering; Q2 and Q3 are festive peaks for consumer-linked IFM and BSS work.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Matrix margin improvement sustainable, and has IFM margin moderation from headcount additions ended?
qa_highlights.answer: EBGC revenue went from INR11.4 crore (Q1 FY26) to INR11.7 crore (Q4 FY26) to INR12.5 crore (Q1 FY27), and gross margin from about 12% to 21%. Management says cost structure is flat, so volume drives margin, and it expects this to hold. IFM EBITDA was INR23.6 crore vs INR23.1 crore YoY, with some cost and contract front-loading.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash balance be used, and are buybacks planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is above INR300 crore across three buckets: inorganic growth, brownfield organic investment, and shareholder rewards. The INR1 interim dividend is the first step. There is no buyback proposal before the Board, though management did not rule one out.

qa_highlights.question: Will the IFM:BSS mix change over 2-3 years, and can agentic AI matter for Athena?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the 67:33 mix to hold, since both segments can grow 9-12%. Agentic AI is in use for outbound lead qualification and inbound repetitive queries. Management said it does not see wholesale replacement of human agents in BFSI near term.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BSS margin fall from 11.5% in Q4 to 7.5% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to a Q4 FY26 Avon restatement that added revenue to last year's Q4. Excluding it, Q4 BSS EBITDA was INR19.1 crore vs INR18.9 crore in Q1, so margins are similar.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the rise in other expenses and the tax-expense swing quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose because of restructuring costs and transport provisions taken in FY26. Tax fell on a manpower-linked tax benefit in a couple of group entities, and the mix is also a factor because Matrix gets no such benefit. Management said the full-year effective tax rate is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the SIS share purchases and the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no discussion with SIS beyond public knowledge; it reads the purchases as a treasury investment. The promoter family holds 59.1%. The acquisition is on hold over valuation.
